raw_response:
My name is Wang — everyone in the village knows me. I have been working these fields since I was fifteen, since before my children were born. Eight mu is not much, but I know every corner of it, and I have kept this family fed for forty-eight years.

Let me think through this year, crop by crop.

---

**Wheat — 4 mu, the flat plot by the road**

I plant wheat every year. Same field, same timing — around Hanlu, when the air turns cold. I use seed I kept from last year's harvest. No need to buy new seed unless something goes wrong with the yield; the old kind grows fine here.

Before planting, I put down about one bag of the black compound fertilizer per mu and mix it in when I till — that is what my mother did and it works. Last year my wheat went yellowish at jointing, so I went back and topdressed with half a bag of urea per mu to green it up. It came back nicely. This year I will do the same without waiting to see if it yellows first. My neighbor across the path says the same: better to put a little extra in spring than to watch it go pale and stand around doing nothing.

Water for wheat, I do three times: once in late fall if the ground is dry after planting, once at jointing, and once at heading. Those last two I never skip. The pump costs money by the hour but skipping heading water would cost me more in lost grain — I know that from one bad year when money was very tight.

At harvest in June I hire the combine. One morning and the 4 mu is done. Then I have to move fast.

---

**Maize — 4 mu, same field, right after wheat**

No time to rest after wheat. Once the combine finishes, I have a few days to get maize in before it is too late in the season. My son-in-law helps when he can come. We hire the planting machine. I buy hybrid maize seed from the market — everyone does now, and the old saved seed cannot keep up.

Fertilizer is similar to wheat. One bag compound per mu in the row at planting, and then I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu when the plant reaches about waist-high — that is when maize is hungry. Last summer was dry and I pumped water once in August. This year I will wait and see. If August brings rain like two years ago, I may not need to pump at all.

Maize harvest the family does together. With eleven people in the house there are enough hands.

---

**Cotton — 3 mu, the west plots**

Cotton is hard work. Picking in September and October is the worst of it — bending over day after day pulling cotton off the bolls. My back is not what it was at forty. But cotton brings cash, I know how to grow it, and I do not know what else to put on those west plots, so I keep 3 mu.

I plant around Guyu — late April. Cotton needs more attention than wheat. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, a little less per mu than wheat because cotton roots go deep. Then twice in summer I add urea: once when the squares start forming, once when the bolls are setting. I water twice — once if spring is dry, once in the summer heat.

Pests with cotton, I watch carefully. Worms and aphids every year. I spray when I see them, not on a schedule. Forty-eight years of watching tells me when.

---

**Mungbean — 1 mu, the back plot behind the house**

The back plot has sandy soil, not as good for wheat. My mother always grew mungbeans there and I do the same. We eat some, sell some at the market. No need for much fertilizer — a little compound at planting is enough. No irrigation needed either; the summer rains usually take care of it. The grandchildren help pick when school is out.

---

**What I am thinking about this year**

My biggest worry is the cotton price. I heard at the market it has been low lately. But I am sixty-three years old and I am not going to learn something completely new for those 3 mu. I will grow cotton and hope the price comes back up.

Cash is always a concern. Fertilizer, seed, the pump, the machines — all of it together runs close to 5,000 yuan before any harvest comes in. My son sends money from the city some months, and his wife helps pick cotton, so I manage. But I do not borrow if I can help it. I do not like owing people money.
